name: Scope Management Plan
purpose: The scope management plan is part of the project management plan and specifies how scope will be defined, developed, monitored, controlled and validated. At least it covers developing a detailed scope statement, decomposing the project into deliverables with a WBS, deciding what is a scope change versus a revision, maintaining the WBS and scope baseline, and accepting deliverables. It is developed once and does not usually change. It may also direct what a WBS Dictionary should contain and how the scope and requirements management plans interact.

elements.guidance: Describe the WBS and whether it is arranged by phases, geography, major deliverables or another way. The guidelines for establishing control accounts and work packages can also go here.
Identify what information is documented in the WBS Dictionary and the level of detail required.
Identify which types of scope change must go through formal change control and how the scope baseline is maintained.
For each deliverable, say how it will be validated for customer acceptance, including any tests or documentation needed for sign-off.
Describe how project and product requirements are addressed in the scope statement and WBS; identify the integration points and how requirements and scope validation will occur.

elements.element: Project management and business analysis integration
elements.guidance: Describe how business analysis and project management integrate as scope is defined, developed, tested, validated and turned over to operations. The blank form does not print this element.

tailoring: On smaller projects, combine the scope management plan with the requirements management plan.
On larger projects, consider a test and evaluation plan that defines how deliverables are validated and accepted by the customer.
If the project involves business analysis, incorporate how business analysis and project management activities interact.
If using an agile or adaptive development approach, incorporate information on the release and iteration plans.
agile_or_adaptive: If an agile or adaptive development approach is used, incorporate information on the release and iteration plans (Tailoring Tips, PDF page 41, printed page 30).
